newsitem.title: CHINA: Diesel smuggling hits profits of Chinese oil firms.
newsitem.headline: Diesel smuggling hits profits of Chinese oil firms.

text.p: Smuggling and other unofficial imports of diesel fuel have hit profits of state-owned oil firms in southern and eastern China, oil officials and state media said on Friday.
The trade has forced domestic retail diesel prices lower, in some cases below the government-set wholesale price at which refiners are supposed to sell.
This has put a financial strain on a number of oil firms under the state oil refiner, China Petrochemical Corp (Sinopec), traders said.
Retail prices in southern and eastern China were just 1,900 yuan per tonne compared with current ex-refinery diesel price of 2,190 yuan per tonne, they said.
Besides smuggling, unofficial imports included diesel brought in legally to bonded storage terminals or by foreign joint ventures for their own use. This fuel has been found on the domestic market.
Smuggled diesel could save about 530 yuan per tonne in duties and taxes.

The Fujian Petroleum Corp in the southeastern province of Fujian had a 9.0 million yuan loss in the first four months of this year while sales of Jiangsu Petroleum Corp in eastern Jiangsu province fell by one-third from the same period of last year, the Business Daily said.
The newspaper linked the problems to smuggling.
"We sold 40,000-50,000 tonnes a month last year, but we sold just 600 tonnes in April and almost nothing in May," an official of the Zhejiang Petroleum Corp in east China told Reuters by telephone.
"Oil wholesalers at all levels in our province have suffered losses," the official said.
Oil wholesalers and distributors under Sinopec must protect the interests of refiners by buying diesel at 2,190 yuan per tonne from refineries, even though they sell the fuel at lower prices.
"The smuggling is seriously upsetting the domestic market," said the Zhejiang refinery official.
About 150,000 tonnes of smuggled diesel have been brought in through eastern coastal Zhejiang province every month this year, he said.
The Business Daily said Zhejiang authorities had seized two boats carrying a combined 1,000 tonnes of diesel in April.
The Zhejiang company official said smuggling was becoming worse and the government needed to take tougher action.
